'''Jeremy Raymon Pargo''' (born March 17, 1986) is an American professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]]. In [[2010–11 Euroleague|2011]] he reached the [[EuroLeague Finals|EuroLeague Final]] with [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]], earning an [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague Second Team]] selection in the process. He was the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League Statistical Leaders#Assists leaders|2015 Israeli Basketball Premier League Assists Leader]], and the 2016 [[Chinese Basketball Association]] assists leader. In 2026, he won the [[Úrvalsdeild karla (basketball)|Icelandic]] championship and was named the [[Úrvalsdeild Men's Playoffs MVP|Úrvalsdeild Playoffs MVP]].

Pargo was a member of the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States national team]] during the [[2022 FIBA AmeriCup]] where he won bronze.

He is the younger brother of former NBA player [[Jannero Pargo]].

==Early life==
Pargo attended [[Chicago]]'s [[Paul Robeson High School (Chicago, Illinois)|Paul Robeson High School]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Jeremy-Pargo-1153/|title=DraftExpress - Jeremy Pargo DraftExpress Profile: Stats, Comparisons, and Outlook|website=DraftExpress}}</ref>

==College career==
Pargo played four seasons of [[college basketball]] for [[Gonzaga University]]'s [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]]. In 2008 in his junior season, he was voted the [[West Coast Conference|WCC]] [[West Coast Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Player of the Year]]. The following year, he was featured on the cover of ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' magazine for the 2009 [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|March Madness]] issue.

During his collegiate career, Pargo averaged 9.3 points, 3.4 rebounds, and 4.3 assists per game. The Bulldogs were very successful during Pargo's time at the school, qualifying for the [[2006 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2006]], [[2007 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2007]], [[2008 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2008]] and [[2009 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2009]] NCAA tournaments.

==Professional career==
===2009–10 season===
After going [[undrafted]] in the [[2009 NBA draft]], Pargo participated in the 2009 Las Vegas [[NBA Summer League]], as a member of the [[Detroit Piston]]s' summer league squad, alongside former [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] teammate [[Austin Daye]].<ref>"2009 NBA Summer League Player Profile – Jeremy Pargo". – ''[[NBA.com]]''. – July 16, 2009,</ref> He also played in the [[Orlando Pro Summer League]] for the [[Orlando Magic]]'s summer league squad. He did not secure a contract, however.

In his first professional year, Pargo played for [[Hapoel Gilboa Galil Elyon]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Super League]], averaging 14.1 points, 2.9 rebounds, 4.5 assists, and 2.7 turnovers per game. He was a home crowd favorite because of his electrifying dunks over bigger defenders. He won the [[2009–10 Israeli Basketball Super League|2009-10 Israeli Super League]] championship.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jeremy Pargo, Basketball Player, News, Stats - Eurobasket |url=https://basketball.eurobasket.com/player/Jeremy-Pargo/89252 |publisher=[[Eurobasket.com]] |access-date=21 April 2025}}</ref>

===2010–11 season===
In 2010, Pargo participated in the [[Orlando Pro Summer League]] for the [[Charlotte Bobcats]], and then later in the Las Vegas [[NBA Summer League]], as a member of the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. On August 26, 2010, Pargo replaced [[Mikhail Torrance]], who was suffering from a heart condition, signing a one-year contract with [[EuroLeague]] giants [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.thehoopsmarket.com/news/maccabi-tel-aviv-signs-jeremy-pargo-to-a-one-year-contract-.aspx |title=Maccabi Tel Aviv signs Jeremy Pargo to a one-year contract. |access-date=August 27, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100829072912/http://www.thehoopsmarket.com/news/maccabi-tel-aviv-signs-jeremy-pargo-to-a-one-year-contract-.aspx |archive-date=August 29, 2010 |url-status=usurped }}</ref> After a promising start, he emerged as one of the team's main players, especially after [[Doron Perkins|Doron Perkins']]s season-ending injury. He helped Maccabi to reach the [[EuroLeague Final]], earning an [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague Second Team]] selection in the process. His team lost in the EuroLeague Finals to [[Panathinaikos BC|Panathinaikos]], by a score of 78–70.

===2011–12 season===
On May 24, 2011, Pargo signed a new two-year contract extension with Maccabi. However, he broke the contract, and on December 10, 2011, he signed a two-year contract with the [[NBA]]'s [[Memphis Grizzlies]], with his successful EuroLeague season not having gone unnoticed.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-sign-jeremy-pargo |title=Grizzlies sign Jeremy Pargo. |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=December 10, 2011 |access-date=December 11, 2011}}</ref>

===2012–13 season===
On July 25, 2012, he was traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], along with a [[2014 NBA Draft|2014]] second round draft pick, in exchange for [[D. J. Kennedy]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/pargo_trade_120725.html |title=Cavaliers Acquire Pargo and 2014 Second Round Pick From Grizzlies. |work=NBA.com |date=July 25, 2012 |access-date=July 26, 2012}}</ref>

On January 22, 2013, Pargo was waived by the Cavaliers.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/trade-130122 |title=Cavaliers Acquire Speights, Ellington, Selby and Future First Round Pick From Grizzlies.|work=NBA.com |date=January 22, 2013 |access-date=February 10, 2013}}</ref>

On February 7, 2013, Pargo was signed to a ten-day contract by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-sign-guard-jeremy-pargo-10-day-contract |title=Sixers Sign Guard Jeremy Pargo to 10-Day Contract.|work=NBA.com |date=February 7, 2013 |access-date=February 10, 2013}}</ref> On February 18, 2013, Pargo was signed by the 76ers for the rest of the 2012–13 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/130218-pargo-signed |title=Sixers Sign Guard Jeremy Pargo For Remainder Of Season.|work=NBA.com |date=February 18, 2013 |access-date=February 19, 2013}}</ref> He was waived on April 1, 2013, when the team signed [[Justin Holiday]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-sign-justin-holiday-and-waive-jeremy-pargo|title=Sixers Sign Justin Holiday and Waive Jeremy Pargo - THE OFFICIAL SITE OF THE PHILADELPHIA 76ERS|website=www.nba.com}}</ref>

===2013–14 season===
[[File:Jeremy Pargo - CSKA Moscow, EuroLeague, 17 October 2013 - 18 (cropped).JPG|thumb|Pargo with CSKA Moscow, 2013]]
In June 2013, he signed a two-year contract worth $5.2 million [[net income]] ([[Euro|€]]4 million) with the Russian club [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://tracking.si.com/2013/06/11/jeremy-pargo-moscow-cska-nba/|title=Jeremy Pargo signs two-year, $5.2M deal with CSKA Moscow.|access-date=June 11, 2013|archive-date=June 15, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130615052415/http://tracking.si.com/2013/06/11/jeremy-pargo-moscow-cska-nba/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===2014–15 season===
On July 24, 2014, Pargo and [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]] reached an agreement to part ways. Later that day, Pargo signed a two-year deal with his former club [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Maccabi brings Pargo back on two-year deal|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/139813/180|website=euroleague.net|access-date=July 24, 2014}}</ref>

===2015–16 season===
On July 4, 2015, he parted ways with Maccabi, signing with the Chinese club [[Zhejiang Lions]] for the [[2015–16 CBA season]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Zhejiang Guangsha officially sign Jeremy Pargo|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/167077/zhejiang-guangsha-officially-sign-jeremy-pargo.html|access-date=July 4, 2015|work=Sportando.com|date=July 4, 2015}}</ref>
On April 27, 2016, Pargo joined the Italian club [[Reyer Venezia Mestre|Reyer Venezia]], for the remainder of the 2015–16 season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 27, 2016 |title=Jeremy Pargo to Reyer Venezia |url=http://www.eurohoops.net/legabasket/233387/jeremy-pargo-to-reyer-venezia |access-date=2025-05-26 |website=Eurohoops}}</ref>

===2016–17 season===
In July 2016, Pargo signed with the Chinese club [[Shenzhen Leopards]].<ref>{{cite news|title=DongGuan Leopards land Jeremy Pargo, ex Umana VE|url=http://www.asia-basket.com/China/news/454078/DongGuan-Leopards-land-Jeremy-Pargo,-ex-Umana-VE|work=Asia-Basket.com|date=July 16, 2016|access-date=October 2, 2016}}</ref>

===2017–18 season===
On December 12, 2017, Pargo signed with the Chinese club [[Nanjing Monkey King]].<ref>{{cite news|title=同曦官方宣布更换外援 前CBA助攻王加盟|url=http://sports.sina.com.cn/cba/2017-12-12/doc-ifypnyqi4301233.shtml|work=Sina.com|language=zh|date=December 12, 2017|access-date=December 13, 2017}}</ref>

On February 26, 2018, Pargo joined the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] of the [[NBA G League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://santacruz.gleague.nba.com/news/santa-cruz-warriors-acquire-guard-jeremy-pargo-off-waivers/|title=Santa Cruz Warriors Acquire Guard Jeremy Pargo Off Waivers|work=NBA.com|date=February 26, 2018|access-date=March 2, 2018|archive-date=March 2, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180302225751/http://santacruz.gleague.nba.com/news/santa-cruz-warriors-acquire-guard-jeremy-pargo-off-waivers/|url-status=dead}}</ref> One month later, Pargo signed with the Lebanese team [[Champville SC]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Jeremy Pargo signs with Champville|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/asia/lebanon/269570/jeremy-pargo-signs-with-champville.html|access-date=March 29, 2018|work=Sportando.com|date=March 28, 2018}}{{Dead link|date=November 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

On April 25, 2018, Pargo returned for a third stint in [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]], signing for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite news|title=הוא חוזר: ג'רמי פארגו חתם במכבי|url=http://maccabi.co.il/news.asp?id=6545|access-date=April 25, 2018|work=maccabi.co.il|language=he|date=April 25, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Jeremy Pargo returns to Maccabi Tel Aviv|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/europe/israel/272515/jeremy-pargo-returns-to-maccabi-tel-aviv.html|access-date=April 26, 2018|work=Sportando.com|date=April 26, 2018}}{{Dead link|date=March 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> On May 17, 2018, Pargo recorded 26 points, scoring 20 points in the fourth quarter, along with four rebounds and four assists, leading Maccabi to a 98–95 win over [[Ironi Nes Ziona]]. He was subsequently named [[2017–18 Israeli Basketball Premier League#MVP of the Round|Israeli League Round 32 MVP]].<ref>{{cite news|title=מצטיין המחזור ה-32: ג'רמי פארגו|url=http://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=18966|access-date=May 19, 2018|work=basket.co.il|date=May 19, 2018|language=he}}</ref> On June 8, 2018, Pargo was named [[2017–18 Israeli Basketball Premier League#Quarterfinals MVP|2018 Israeli League Quarterfinals MVP]].<ref>{{cite news|title=מצטייני עונת 2017/18 בליגת ווינר סל|url=http://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=19053|access-date=June 8, 2018|work=basket.co.il|date=June 8, 2018|language=he}}</ref> Pargo made a key contribution to Maccabi's [[2018 Israeli Basketball Premier League Final Four|2018 Israeli League Championship]] title.

===2018–19 season===
On July 11, 2018, Pargo signed a one-year contract extension with Maccabi Tel Aviv.<ref>{{cite news|title=Maccabi re-signs guard Pargo|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/8v89qn5kip8qynql/maccabi-re-signs-guard-pargo|access-date=July 11, 2018|work=EuroLeague.net|date=July 11, 2018}}</ref> Pargo won the [[2019 Israeli Basketball Premier League Final Four|2019 Israeli League Championship]] with Maccabi, winning the Israeli League title for two consecutive years.

===2019–20 season===
On November 7, 2019, Pargo joined the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] of the [[NBA G League]] for a second stint.<ref>{{cite news|title=Santa Cruz Warriors Announce 2019-20 Opening Night Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/santa-cruz-warriors-announce-2019-20-opening-night-roster/n-5569155|access-date=November 8, 2019|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=November 7, 2019}}</ref> He scored 37 points against the [[South Bay Lakers]] on December 10.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Seimas |first1=Jim |title=Jeremy Pargo scores 34 points as Santa Cruz storms past Iowa |url=https://www.santacruzsentinel.com/2020/01/15/jeremy-pargo-scores-34-points-as-santa-cruz-storms-past-iowa-g-league-basketball/ |access-date=January 16, 2020 |work=[[Santa Cruz Sentinel]] |date=January 15, 2020}}</ref>

On February 8, 2020, Pargo signed a 10-day contract with the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Warriors Sign Guards Zach Norvell Jr. and Jeremy Pargo to 10-Day Contracts|url= https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/pargo-norvell-10day-contracts-20200208|date=February 8, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 8, 2020}}</ref> In his debut the same day against the Lakers, Pargo appeared in an NBA game for the first time in six years, 316 days — the sixth-longest gap between game appearances in NBA history. Pargo posted 15 points in a 112–106 loss to the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Letourneau |first1=Connor |title='He's an NBA player': Warriors' Jeremy Pargo proving his worth |url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/warriors/article/He-s-an-NBA-player-How-Warriors-15063183.php |access-date=May 18, 2020 |work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]] |date=February 17, 2020}}</ref>

===2020–21 season===
On June 3, 2020, Pargo signed with [[Hapoel Jerusalem]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Hapoel Jerusalem announces Jeremy Pargo |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/hapoel-jerusalem-announces-jeremy-pargo/ |website=Sportando |access-date=June 4, 2020 |date=June 3, 2020}}</ref>

On February 15, 2021, he signed with [[Maccabi Rishon LeZion (basketball)|Maccabi Rishon LeZion]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/jeremy-pargo-signs-with-maccabi-rishon-lezion/|title=Jeremy Pargo signs with Maccabi Rishon LeZion|last=|first=|date=February 15, 2021|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=February 16, 2021}}</ref>

===2021–22 season===
On November 1, 2021, Pargo signed with [[Napoli Basket (2016)|Napoli Basket]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA).<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/gevi-napoli-announces-jeremy-pargo/|title=GeVi Napoli announces Jeremy Pargo|date=November 1, 2021|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=November 1, 2021|last1=Maggi |first1=Alessandro }}</ref> On January 10, 2022, he was traded from the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] to the [[Windy City Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League transactions|date=January 10, 2022|access-date=January 10, 2022}}</ref> Napoli and Pargo mutually parted ways on January 25, allowing him to return to the USA. He averaged 9.6 points and 3.6 assists per game in his tenure with the Italian team.<ref>{{cite news |title=Gevi Napoli Basket, Jeremy Pargo part ways |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/gevi-napoli-basket-jeremy-pargo-part-ways/ |website=Sportando |access-date=January 25, 2022 |date=January 25, 2022|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }}</ref>

===2022–23 season===
On January 1, 2023, Pargo was reacquired by the [[Windy City Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2022-23 NBA G League Transactions|date=January 1, 2023|access-date=January 1, 2023}}</ref> On April 11, 2023, he signed with [[Real Betis Baloncesto|Real Betis]] of the [[Liga ACB]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/jeremy-pargo-joins-real-betis-baloncesto/|title=Jeremy Pargo joins Real Betis Baloncesto|date=April 11, 2023|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=April 12, 2023 |last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano }}</ref>

===2023–24 season===
On August 28, 2023, Pargo signed with the [[NBA G League Ignite]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ignite Announces Veteran Roster Additions For 2023-24 Season|url=https://ignite.gleague.nba.com/news/ignite-announces-veteran-roster-additions-for-2023-24-season|website=NBA.com|date=August 28, 2023|access-date=August 28, 2023|archive-date=August 29, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230829024823/https://ignite.gleague.nba.com/news/ignite-announces-veteran-roster-additions-for-2023-24-season|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Grindavík (2025–2026)===
In January 2025, Pargo signed with [[Grindavík men's basketball|Grindavík]] of the [[Úrvalsdeild karla (basketball)|Úrvalsdeild karla]].<ref>{{cite news |author1=Sindri Sverrisson |title=Grindavík fær félaga Kane sem spilaði í NBA |url=https://www.visir.is/g/20252680379d/grindavik-faer-felaga-kane-sem-spiladi-i-nba |access-date=27 January 2025 |work=[[Vísir.is]] |date=26 January 2025 |language=Icelandic}}</ref> In his debut, he scored 25 point in a 95–104 win against [[Þór Þorlákshöfn (basketball club)|Þór Þorlákshöfn]].<ref>{{cite news |author1=Ágúst Orri Arnarson |title="Meiri ró og betri ára yfir Grindavík" með Jeremy Pargo |url=https://www.visir.is/g/20252686146d/-meiri-ro-og-betri-ara-yfir-grindavik-med-jeremy-pargo |access-date=10 February 2025 |work=[[Vísir.is]] |date=9 February 2025 |language=Icelandic}}</ref> He appeared in six regular season games where he averaged 25.7 points, 4.3 rebounds and 7.3 assists. In the first round of the playoffs, he helped Grindavík knock out reigning national champions [[Valur men's basketball|Valur]], 3–1.<ref>{{cite news |author1=Hjörtur Leó Guðjónsson |title=Uppgjörið: Grindavík - Valur 82-74 - Meistararnir sendir í sumarfrí |url=https://www.visir.is/g/20252714827d/leik-lokid-grindavik-valur-82-74-meistararnir-sendir-i-sumarfri |access-date=21 April 2025 |work=[[Vísir.is]] |date=14 April 2025 |language=Icelandic}}</ref>

After not starting the 2025–2026 season with Grindavík, he rejoined the team in January 2026, replacing [[Khalil Shabazz]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Grindavík tilkynnir eftirmann Khalil Shabazz |url=https://www.karfan.is/grindavik-tilkynnir-eftirmann-khalil-shabazz/ |access-date=30 January 2026 |work=Karfan.is |date=30 January 2026 |language=Icelandic}}</ref> He played the final six games of the regular season, helping Grindavík to the best record in the league.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Grindavík deildarmeistari |url=https://www.mbl.is/sport/korfubolti/2026/03/13/grindavik_deildarmeistari/ |access-date=2026-05-13 |website=www.mbl.is |language=is}}</ref> On 18 May 2026, he won the Icelandic championship and was named the [[Úrvalsdeild Men's Playoffs MVP|Playoffs MVP]] after Grindavík defeated Tindastóll 3-1 in the Úrvalsdeild finals. With starters [[Ólafur Ólafsson]], [[Deandre Kane]] and [[Daniel Mortensen]] out due to injures, Pargo scored 48 points in the championship clinching game, making 10 of 16 three point shots.<ref>{{cite news |author1=Aron Guðmundsson |title=Þakkaði guði eftir leik sem gæti verið hans síðasti |url=https://www.visir.is/g/20262885900d/thakkadi-gudi-eftir-leik-sem-gaeti-verid-hans-sidasti |access-date=19 May 2026 |work=[[Vísir.is]] |date=18 May 2026|lang=IS}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author1=Sindri Sverrisson |title=Sjáðu öll tilþrif Pargo: „Aldrei séð annað eins á fjölum á Íslandi“ |url=https://www.visir.is/g/20262885963d/sjadu-oll-tilthrif-pargo-aldrei-sed-annad-eins-a-fjolum-a-islandi- |access-date=19 May 2026 |work=[[Vísir.is]] |date=19 May 2026 |language=Icelandic}}</ref>

===The Basketball Tournament===
In the summer of 2017, Pargo played in [[The Basketball Tournament]] (TBT)—a single-elimination winner-take-all tournament—for team Few Good Men (Gonzaga alumni). He averaged 13.3 points per game (PPG) and helped take the team to the Super 16 round of [[The Basketball Tournament 2017|TBT 2017]], where they lost to Team Challenge ALS, 77–60. In [[The Basketball Tournament 2018|TBT 2018]], Pargo played for [[Overseas Elite]], the three-time defending champion. In six games, he averaged 7.7 PPG, 3.3 assists per game and 2.3 rebounds per game. Overseas Elite reached the championship game and defeated [[Eberlein Drive]], 70–58, for their fourth consecutive TBT title. In [[The Basketball Tournament 2019|TBT 2019]], Pargo and Overseas Elite advanced to the semifinals where they suffered their first-ever defeat, losing to [[Carmen's Crew]], 71–66.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://thetournament.com/news/1-carmens-crew-71-1-overseas-elite-66 |title=#1 Carmen's Crew 71, #1 Overseas Elite 66 |website=thetournament.com |date=August 4, 2019 |access-date=August 4, 2019 |archive-date=January 23, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200123041911/http://www.thetournament.com/news/1-carmens-crew-71-1-overseas-elite-66 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===3-on-3 basketball===
In 2026, Pargo joined [[Boston Ball Hogs]] of the [[BIG3]].<ref>{{cite news |author1=Óskar Ófeigur Jónsson |title=Gary Payton þjálfar Jeremy Pargo í BIG3-deildinni |url=https://www.visir.is/g/20262909381d/gary-payton-thjalfar-jeremy-pargo-i-big3-deildinni |access-date=19 July 2026 |work=[[Vísir.is]] |date=14 July 2026 |language=Icelandic}}</ref>

On 22nd August 2026, Pargo hit a 4-Point shot to overcome a 2-point deficit and win the BIG3 Championship.

==National team career==
Pargo played for the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States national team]] during the [[2022 FIBA AmeriCup]] where the team finished third. He appeared in 6 games, averaging 8.8 points and 5.7 assists per game.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jeremy Pargo - USA - Player profile - FIBA AmeriCup |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/history/184-fiba-americup/9552/players/177043-jeremy-pargo |website=fiba.basketball |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=23 December 2025}}</ref>
